personas.label: 免费碎片旅行对话
utterances: Hi! I'm visiting London for the first time. I get a bit nervous when I have to ask someone for help.
I have a small notebook with addresses, but I would like to practise asking for directions instead of looking at my phone.
This morning I took the wrong train. I got off at the next station and walked back along the river.
I didn't understand the announcement. What could I say politely to ask somebody to repeat it?
I want find a quiet place to have lunch. I don't eat meat, and my budget is about twelve pounds.
I often worry about holding up the queue. Then I speak too quickly and forget the words I wanted to use.
Would it sound natural if I said, 'Could I have a little more time to decide, please?'
My friend Lin is joining me later. She likes parks and small museums more than famous shopping streets.
Yesterday we was discussing whether to book everything in advance. I prefer leaving a little room for surprises.
I have only one afternoon free. How would you choose between seeing more places and spending longer in one place?
I think I will choose a neighbourhood and explore it slowly. That feels less stressful than making a long list.
Thanks! Before I go, can you help me say my lunch request once more in a short, natural way?

characters.name: Oliver Bennett
characters.speechStyle: natural conversational English with concrete examples
characters.background: Works in a small London bookshop and grew up in Kent.

utterances: Hi Oliver! I'm new in London and a bit nervous about speaking English.
I walked along the river this morning. It was quieter than I expected.
I want find a little bookshop near here. Do you have a recommendation?
I like stories about ordinary people. What are you reading these days?
I usually read on the train, but sometimes I get distracted by my phone.
Yesterday I buyed a used novel. The notes in the margin were fascinating.
My friend Mei loves old books too. I promised to bring her something home.
Actually, could you explain what you mean in a simpler way?
That makes sense. I'd rather browse slowly than follow a long shopping list.
I used to be afraid of making mistakes, so I stayed quiet in conversations.
Last week I finally asked a stranger for directions without using a translation app.
What would you do if someone couldn't understand your accent?
I'm back! I tried your idea and felt a little more confident.
Do you remember the friend I wanted to buy a book for?
She likes photography as well. I wonder if there's a book combining both interests.
I don't need a perfect gift. I'd like it to feel personal.
Sometimes I worry that spending time alone means I'm missing out on things.
But a quiet afternoon with a book can be exactly what I need.
If I had more time, I would explored a different neighbourhood every day.
Could you tell me about a place that means something to you?
I like hearing those little stories. They make a city feel more real.
I think I'll write Mei a note about how I found her gift.
Before I go, what was the name of the kind of book we were talking about?
Thanks for chatting with me. I'll tell you how the gift goes next time.
